workflow: Parallel phase planners require isolated git worktrees — without them, the GSD branch auto-switch from committing one phase's context yanks the branch out from under an actively-running planner on a different phase

Worktree isolation pattern: checkout main in main tree, git worktree add <path> <branch>, pnpm i in worktree (not symlink — symlink breaks hook isolation), then spawn agent with working dir set to worktree
A backgrounded agent that hits a session/usage limit leaves no error signal — it just stops; always check worktree HEAD advancement to detect stalls vs. active progress
When a planner agent is stopped mid-pipeline (before its first commit), it's safe to restart cleanly — check for uncommitted changes first

The compound-action pattern (discuss inline while plan/execute run in background) works on Claude Code when subagents have Tools: * — the conservative 'run plan inline only' guardrail in manager.md is overly restrictive for this harness
